submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad layer-0 head: predict ordinary prose, code and names active-weak (content nouns, verbs and word fragments near a text's start reach 0.25-0.5 of max; a short plain sentence with no comma or determiner sits near the line, so about a third of those fall just below), and predict it strong (0.6-1.0 of max) on a comma or a determiner (' the', ' a', ' an') within roughly the first five tokens of a text, where it attends mostly to itself; the same tokens fade with position and are usually below the line by token 8-14. Predicted inactive (near 0): the tokens ' and', ' of', ' from', ' by' at any position, and short phrases whose every word is a single-token directional or adverb particle (Up, down, In, out, On, off, Over, under, Back, forth, around, again) joined only by ' and', ' of', ' from' or ' by' (e.g. 'Up and down', 'In and out of', 'Back and forth and back again', 'Up and down and all around'), with no comma, determiner, noun or multi-token word; pairs like 'Ahead and behind', 'Forward and backward', 'Left and right' or 'Near and far' are content or multi-token words and are predicted active-weak.
